story.title: Trump Appoints Stephen Miller as New Chief of Staff Following Midterm Losses
story.summary: Donald Trump has announced that Stephen Miller will replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff. Wiles, who served for 21 months and was the first woman to hold the position, is stepping down after significant Republican losses in the recent midterm elections. Miller, known for his controversial role in shaping the administration's immigration policies, will take on the top advisory role.

explore_lenses.label: What actually changes on Monday?
explore_lenses.title: Miller takes the White House’s top staff role
explore_lenses.summary: Stephen Miller is scheduled to become chief of staff on Monday, November 9, replacing Susie Wiles. The announcement describes a personnel and portfolio change within the White House, not a Cabinet appointment.

claims.text: Trump said Miller, then deputy chief of staff, would become chief of staff on November 9, 2026, and that Wiles would move to the Trump Political Operation.
A July 2026 White House personnel report listed Miller as deputy chief of staff for policy and homeland security adviser, while Wiles was listed as chief of staff.
The White House says the Executive Office of the President is overseen by the chief of staff and that most EOP advisers are appointed with presidential discretion.

points: Trump said Miller, then deputy chief of staff, would become chief of staff on November 9, 2026, and that Wiles would move to the Trump Political Operation.
A July 2026 White House personnel report listed Miller as deputy chief of staff for policy and homeland security adviser, while Wiles was listed as chief of staff.
The White House says the Executive Office of the President is overseen by the chief of staff and that most EOP advisers are appointed with presidential discretion.
explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: The announcement did not specify who will assume Miller’s former policy and homeland-security responsibilities or whether those roles will be formally separated.

explore_lenses.label: Does this itself change immigration policy?
explore_lenses.title: No new immigration action was announced
explore_lenses.summary: Miller’s appointment places an adviser closely associated with the administration’s immigration agenda in the chief-of-staff role, but the announcement did not identify a new immigration order, rule, or operational change.

claims.text: AP reported that Miller has a broad portfolio but is most closely associated with Trump’s immigration policy and immigration rhetoric.
The White House’s July personnel report gave Miller the concurrent titles of deputy chief of staff for policy and homeland security adviser.
Trump characterized Miller as one of his most trusted advisers when announcing the promotion.

explore_lenses.label: How is the change tied to the midterm result?
explore_lenses.title: The move follows, but does not explain, the losses
explore_lenses.summary: Trump announced the replacement days after the November 3 midterms, in which Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress. The available announcement does not state that the election outcome caused Wiles’s reassignment.

claims.text: AP reported that Trump announced the chief-of-staff change days after Republicans lost control of Congress in the midterm elections.
AP reported that Democrats won the House and Senate, ending Republican control of both chambers.
Trump praised Wiles’s work and said she would continue in his political organization, rather than describing her departure as a dismissal or attributing it to the election result.

story_report.summary: President Donald Trump has appointed Stephen Miller to replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff, effective Nov. 9, 2026. Miller, then serving as deputy chief of staff, will take over the post after Wiles’s 21-month tenure. Wiles is set to move to the Trump Political Operation, while the announcement left open who will assume Miller’s previous policy and homeland-security responsibilities. The personnel change was announced days after Democrats won the House and Senate in the midterm elections.

sections.heading: Miller’s White House Portfolio
sections.body: Before the promotion, a July White House personnel report listed Miller as deputy chief of staff for policy and homeland security adviser, alongside Wiles as chief of staff. The chief of staff oversees the Executive Office of the President, according to the White House. AP reported that Miller has held a broad portfolio but is most closely associated with Trump’s immigration policy and rhetoric.

sections.heading: Midterm Context and Wiles’s Move
sections.body: Trump announced the staffing shift days after Republicans lost control of Congress, with Democrats winning both the House and Senate. Trump praised Wiles’s work and said she would continue in his political organization. The announcement did not describe her move as a dismissal or attribute it to the election outcome, and the available reporting does not establish a direct causal link between the midterm losses and her reassignment.

unresolved.text: The announcement did not specify who will take over Miller’s former policy and homeland-security duties or whether those responsibilities will be formally separated.
The personnel announcement alone does not establish whether Miller’s promotion will lead to changes in immigration policy or enforcement.

related_stories.title: Mass Protests Erupt in Paraguay Over Banking Scandal and Impeachment of President Peña
related_stories.summary: Thousands of Paraguayans are protesting against a banking scandal that has left nearly half the population unable to access their savings. Demonstrators are calling for the impeachment of President Santiago Peña, who has offered to resign amid the crisis. However, Congress has put his resignation on hold as impeachment proceedings continue.

related_stories.title: Former West Virginia Governor and Senator Jay Rockefeller Dies at 89
related_stories.summary: Jay Rockefeller, the last member of his family's political dynasty, has died at the age of 89. He served as West Virginia's governor and was a long-time U.S. senator, known for his advocacy in health care and public service in one of the nation's poorest states.

related_stories.title: Amateur Cricketer 'Clicky Ponting' Receives Two-Year Ban for Cheating
related_stories.summary: An amateur cricketer known as 'Clicky Ponting' has been banned from cricket for two years due to cheating during matches. He was found to have been clicking his fingers while fielding to deceive the umpire into believing that the batsman had edged the ball.
